name: Vegetable juices, root-vegetable-containing
anchor: Per-form sovereign beverage cells in the as-consumed liquid basis (EU 2023/915 juice and rice-drink cells, Codex CXS 193 fruit juices, EU 2024/1987 beverage nickel, EU canned-beverage tin, Hong Kong Cap 132V's named carbonated, tea, coffee and wine beverage entries, and the US and Hong Kong packaged-drinking-water quality standards), with dry leaf, bean and powder commodities anchored separately in their own as-sold basis and never converted between the two
native_basis_label: ready-to-drink liquid, as consumed (wet weight, single strength); a concentrate or a powder-to-liquid product is assessed as reconstituted to single strength per the manufacturer's own directions, which is the basis EU 2023/915 and Codex CXS 193 write into their juice cells and Hong Kong Cap 132V Note 11 writes into its beverage entries
scope_note: Single-strength ready-to-drink vegetable juices and blends whose vegetable content includes a root or tuber vegetable: beetroot, carrot, celeriac, parsnip, turnip, radish, ginger and turmeric. The row is split out because root and tuber vegetables are the direct soil-uptake interface for cadmium and lead and because credible sovereigns write a distinct root-and-tuber cadmium cell for exactly that reason; a root-vegetable juice must not inherit a fruit or leafy-vegetable anchor by default. A juice with no root or tuber content routes to the non-root row. Single-ingredient root-vegetable products for children under two are Category 1 and are excluded from this row's anchor set by the taxonomy boundary rule.
basis_guard: as[ _]consumed|wet weight|reconstituted|ready.to.drink|product as placed on market|\bjuice\b|portion ordinarily consumed|food as listed in Cap 132V Part 2 Schedule
basis_guard_note: This row's anchors span two wet, edible-portion bases, and the guard is written against the two fields the compiler actually tests, which are the register's basis and basis_class. The beverage anchors (lead, inorganic arsenic, nickel, tin) are ready-to-drink cells admitted through as consumed, wet weight, reconstituted, ready to drink, product as placed on market, or juice. The source-commodity anchors (cadmium, total mercury, total arsenic, total chromium) are Hong Kong Cap 132V Part 2 Schedule entries, admitted through the explicit Cap 132V basis string rather than through a bare as-sold token. That distinction is deliberate. An earlier form of this guard carried a bare as_sold alternative, which admitted any register row whose basis_class was as_sold regardless of instrument or commodity, including dry-leaf, dry-bean and dry-grain cells from other categories; the bare token has been removed and the widening is now tied to the one instrument that needs it. Two limits of the guard are stated rather than overclaimed. First, the Cap 132V alternative admits every Part 2 Schedule entry, dry entries included, because the register records an identical basis string for the whole schedule and encodes no product form in either basis field; a Cap 132V dry-commodity entry is therefore kept off this row by the named-anchor discipline and by this row's audit scope, not by the guard, and every Cap 132V anchor named on this row is disclosed on the face of its cell together with the Part 2 commodity it is written for. Second, the guard refuses dry-matter, dry-weight, feed, migration and article-content bases only where the instrument's own basis string says so; it cannot refuse a dry commodity whose register basis omits those words, and it is not represented as doing so. The commodity-to-juice read-across is taken at face value with no concentration, reconstitution or dry-matter factor applied in either direction, and that treatment is disclosed on each cell that relies on it.
method: HMTc Method v2.0 (government-limit-only): the strictest applicable sovereign maximum level for this exact beverage form and analyte in the row's declared native basis, with disclosed read-across where the exact cell is unregulated, a substantiated not-material determination where a species is bounded or is a method artifact, and a control where no defensible sovereign number and no supportable near-neighbour exist. Never occurrence-derived. Ready-to-drink and dry-commodity bases are never mixed and no brewing, dilution or reconstitution factor is invented.

Pb.basis: wet weight, single-strength ready-to-drink juice (read across from the EU fruit-juice cell)
Pb.source_scope: fruit juices, fruit juices from concentrate, concentrated fruit juices, and fruit nectars other than exclusively from berries and other small fruits
Pb.label: No credible sovereign has written a lead maximum level for vegetable juice: EU 2023/915 section 3.1.19, Codex CXS 193 and Hong Kong Cap 132V all scope their juice lead cells to FRUIT juices and nectars. The nearest applicable sovereign value is therefore the EU fruit-juice lead cell (30 ug/kg) in the identical single-strength ready-to-drink basis, and it is adopted by disclosed read-across.
Pb.substantiation: The alternative candidate set was the source-vegetable commodity cells, and every one of them is looser: EU 2023/915 sets root and tuber vegetables at 100 ug/kg, Hong Kong Cap 132V sets the same commodity at 100 ug/kg, and FSANZ Schedule 19 sets vegetables except brassicas at 100 ug/kg. Adopting the beverage-form cell at 30 ug/kg is both the nearer form analog (a juice read across to a juice, with no basis change) and the more protective choice, and the looser commodity cells are disclosed here so the selection is auditable rather than asserted. No occurrence data was consulted in selecting the value; the number is the EU's, unchanged.

Cd.basis: fresh-weight edible portion of the source root or tuber vegetable, read across to the single-strength juice at face value with no concentration or dilution factor applied

components.basis: food as listed in Cap 132V Part 2 Schedule; source unit mg/kg

Cd.label: No credible sovereign has written a cadmium maximum level for vegetable juice. Three credible sovereigns converge on 100 ug/kg for the root and tuber vegetable commodity that defines this row, and that value is adopted by disclosed read-across to the juice.
Cd.substantiation: Root and tuber vegetables are the cadmium-relevant commodity family for this row, and EU 2023/915, Hong Kong Cap 132V and FSANZ Schedule 19 all set 100 ug/kg for it: the convergence removes any single-regulator-outlier objection. The read-across is a form change (whole root to its juice), and the basis treatment is stated precisely rather than glossed. The binding anchor eu2023_cd_root_tuber_vegetables_100 is recorded in the register on a wet-weight basis, so for the cell that actually binds there is no basis change at all. The two corroborating cells are recorded differently, Hong Kong Cap 132V as an as-sold Part 2 Schedule entry and FSANZ Schedule 19 as the portion ordinarily consumed, and each is compared to the single-strength juice at face value. No concentration, dilution or dry-matter factor is applied in either direction to any member of the candidate set. The stricter Hong Kong Cap 132V cadmium cells at 50 ug/kg were considered and are NOT adopted here, and they are named so the rejection is auditable rather than implied: cucurbit fruiting vegetables (hk_cap132v_cd_fruiting-vegetables-cucurbits_50), fruiting vegetables other than cucurbits and tomatoes (hk_cap132v_cd_fruiting-vegetables-other-than-cucurbits-and-tomatoes_50), bulb vegetables (hk_cap132v_cd_bulb-vegetables_50) and brassica vegetables other than brassica leafy vegetables (hk_cap132v_cd_brassica-vegetables-other-than-brassica-leafy-vegetable_50). Each is written for a botanical family that is not a root or tuber, while this row is defined by its root and tuber content and the same regulator wrote a separate, named root-and-tuber cell for exactly that commodity. Adopting a neighbouring family cell over the commodity own named cell would be reaching past the instrument rather than applying it. Where a blend content is predominantly bulb or brassica rather than root or tuber it is not certified in this row at all: it routes to the non-root row, whose ceiling is 50 ug/kg. Where a blend's non-root vegetable fraction predominates, the non-root row and its 50 ug/kg ceiling apply instead. Cadmium carries mandatory lot testing and Standards Ratchet surveillance under Governance Policy section 12; no occurrence data selected the number.

tAs.screen_note: Total arsenic is recorded as a SCREEN and not as a protective standalone ceiling. The health-relevant species in this product form is inorganic arsenic, which this row caps at 20 ug/kg; a total-arsenic value twenty-five times higher cannot be protective on its own, and it is published because a credible sovereign wrote a total-arsenic maximum level for the source commodity, not because it describes a safe level. The binding health control in this row is the inorganic-arsenic cell together with the speciation reflex recorded below.
tAs.binding_control: Total arsenic by ICP-MS on every certified lot. Inorganic-arsenic speciation (HPLC-ICP-MS) is reflexed whenever total arsenic exceeds 10 ug/kg, which is 50 percent of this row's inorganic-arsenic ceiling, and the 20 ug/kg inorganic-arsenic ceiling then binds independently of the screen value. Species never substitute for totals and totals never substitute for species: the iAs result does not satisfy the tAs reporting requirement, and compliance with the 500 ug/kg total-arsenic screen does not satisfy the inorganic-arsenic ceiling.
tAs.basis: fresh-weight edible portion of the source vegetable (Hong Kong Cap 132V Part 2 Schedule, which the register records as an as-sold commodity cell), read across to the single-strength juice at face value with no concentration or dilution factor applied; total arsenic
tAs.label: Hong Kong Cap 132V Part 2 item 2 sets arsenic, expressed as total arsenic, in vegetables at 500 ug/kg. No credible sovereign has written an unspeciated arsenic maximum level for vegetable juice itself, so the source-commodity cell is adopted by disclosed read-across from the same instrument and on the same logic as this row's cadmium anchor, and it is recorded as a screen.
tAs.substantiation: The candidate set and the rejections. Regulators write beverage arsenic limits on the inorganic species (EU 2023/915 section 3.4.4 fruit juices at 20 ug/kg and section 3.4.1.6 non-alcoholic rice-based drinks at 30 ug/kg; the US FDA apple-juice action level at 10 ug/kg), and the unspeciated beverage arsenic values that exist sit in the packaged-water schedules (US 21 CFR 165.110 and Hong Kong Cap 132V packaged drinking water, both 10 ug/kg), which govern water sold as water and are Category 8 instruments. Codex CXS 210 sets total arsenic in named vegetable oils at 100 ug/kg (codex_tas_named-vegetable-oils_100); an oil is a different commodity in a different basis and it does not describe a juice, so it is excluded from this row's scan rather than adopted. Adopting the Hong Kong vegetable cell publishes a sovereign ceiling where this row previously published none, and it loosens nothing: the 20 ug/kg inorganic-arsenic ceiling and the speciation reflex continue to bind, so no lot that would have failed under the previous control disposition can pass under this one. No occurrence data selected the number.

iAs.basis: wet weight, single-strength ready-to-drink juice (read across from the EU fruit-juice cell)
iAs.source_scope: fruit juices, concentrated fruit juices as reconstituted, and fruit nectars
iAs.label: No credible sovereign has written an inorganic-arsenic maximum level for vegetable juice. The nearest applicable sovereign value is the EU 2023/915 section 3.4.4 fruit-juice cell (20 ug/kg) in the identical single-strength ready-to-drink basis, adopted by disclosed read-across.
iAs.substantiation: Arsenic reaches a root-vegetable juice through irrigation water and soil rather than through the fruit-versus-vegetable distinction, so a beverage-form arsenic cell reads across cleanly with no basis change. The US FDA apple-juice action level (10 ug/kg) was considered and rejected as inapplicable: it is scoped to a single named fruit commodity that this row excludes. The EU non-alcoholic rice-based drinks cell (30 ug/kg) was considered and rejected as both looser and scoped to a rice hazard this row does not carry.

tHg.binding_control: Total mercury by ICP-MS, or by dedicated amalgamation atomic absorption spectrometry, on every certified lot and reported on the certificate. The 10 ug/kg ceiling binds. A result above 5 ug/kg, which is 50 percent of the ceiling, escalates to an ingredient and process-water investigation and reflexes methylmercury speciation before release.
tHg.basis: fresh-weight edible portion of the source vegetable (Hong Kong Cap 132V Part 2 Schedule, which the register records as an as-sold commodity cell), read across to the single-strength juice at face value with no concentration or dilution factor applied; total mercury
tHg.label: No credible sovereign has written a total-mercury maximum level for vegetable juice itself, but Hong Kong Cap 132V Part 2 item 12 sets mercury, expressed as total mercury, in vegetables other than edible fungi at 10 ug/kg, and that is the source-commodity cell for a root-vegetable-containing juice. It is adopted by disclosed read-across from the same instrument and on the same logic as this row's cadmium anchor: mercury reaches a vegetable juice through the vegetable, so the source-commodity cell is the nearest applicable sovereign value.
tHg.substantiation: The candidate set and the rejections. The packaged-drinking-water quality standards (US 21 CFR 165.110 total mercury at 2 ug/kg; Hong Kong Cap 132V packaged drinking water, written for inorganic mercury at 6 ug/kg) are stricter but govern water sold as water and are Category 8 instruments; a single-strength vegetable juice is not water sold as water, and this row does not reach into the packaged-water schedules for a number. The fish and seafood methylmercury and total-mercury ceilings describe a marine bioaccumulation pathway that this supply chain does not have. Outside the credible-regulator set, Israel's beverages, juices and nectars total-mercury cell (il_fcs2016_thg_17_1_beverages_juices_and_nectars_10) reaches this exact product form and carries the identical 10 ug/kg value; it is recorded here as corroboration that the adopted number is the one a regulator writing for this form arrives at, and it is not used as an anchor. Adopting the Hong Kong vegetable cell publishes a sovereign ceiling where this row previously published none, and it removes nothing: total mercury remains a mandatory lot test and the escalation rule below continues to bind. No occurrence data selected the number; the number is Hong Kong's, unchanged.

companions.basis: food as listed in Cap 132V Part 2 Schedule; source unit mg/kg
companions.scope: Bottled or packaged drinking waters, other than natural mineral waters

MeHg.rationale: Methylmercury has no formation pathway in a root-vegetable-containing juice: there is no marine bioaccumulation step in the supply chain and no anaerobic, sulfate-reducing methylation environment in the product or its process. Methylmercury is a component of total mercury (MeHg <= tHg) and is governed by and bounded by the total-mercury cell; no separate methylmercury ceiling is published.
MeHg.reference_method: Bounded by the total-mercury cell (tHg). Methylmercury speciation (HPLC-ICP-MS or GC-ICP-MS) is reflexed only on an elevated total-mercury result; it is not a routine lot test for this form.
MeHg.regulatory_basis: No credible sovereign sets a methylmercury limit for any beverage, leaf, bean or beverage powder. Methylmercury maximum levels are scoped to fish, seafood and other marine matrices (EU 2023/915 section 3.3, US FDA CPG 540.600, Hong Kong Cap 132V fish entries). Methylmercury is a species of and bounded by total mercury (MeHg <= tHg), which this row controls directly.
MeHg.jurisdictions_checked: EU 2023/915 (and EU 2024/1987 for nickel, EU 2025/1891 for arsenic in seafood); Codex CXS 193-1995; US FDA (21 CFR 165.110 bottled-water quality standards, Juice HACCP guidance, Closer to Zero action levels); FSANZ Food Standards Code Schedule 19; Health Canada List of Contaminants and Other Adulterating Substances; UK retained maximum levels; Hong Kong Cap 132V (Food Adulteration (Metallic Contamination) Regulations) — none sets a methylmercury limit for this product form.

Ni.basis: product as placed on market, ready-to-drink liquid
Ni.label: EU 2024/1987 writes its 250 ug/kg nickel cell for fruit AND vegetable juices and nectars generally, so this is a direct sovereign maximum level for a vegetable juice, not a read-across.
Ni.substantiation: Direct regulatory lookup; the instrument names vegetable juices explicitly and applies from 1 July 2025. The listed 1000 ug/kg band is written for passion fruit, cocoa fruit, small fruits and berries and coconut water, none of which is a vegetable juice, so it is not applicable to this row. Nickel is a Tier-2 analyte.

Sn.basis: product as placed on market, ready-to-drink liquid (inorganic tin)
Sn.label: EU 2023/915 Annex I section 3.5.2 sets inorganic tin in canned beverages, including canned fruit and vegetable juices, at 100 mg/kg = 100000 ug/kg; Hong Kong Cap 132V sets canned beverages at 150000 ug/kg. The EU value is the strictest applicable and binds. This is a direct sovereign maximum level on the beverage-in-a-can form, not a read-across.
Sn.substantiation: Tin in a beverage is a tinplate and can-lining migration pathway, so the government instruments are written on the canned form and the canned form is where the hazard sits. The EU cell (100000 ug/kg) directly governs every canned or tinplate-packaged product in this row and is adopted as the row ceiling for all packaging formats; a carton, PET, glass or pouch format has no tin source and complies trivially, so no separate non-canned cell is published. The looser Hong Kong canned-beverage cell (150000) and the canned-foods cells for solid foods (EU 200000; Codex, FSANZ and Hong Kong 250000) are disclosed and deliberately not adopted: EU writes a stricter cell specifically for beverages and HMTc preserves that product-form split. Tin is a Tier-2 analyte; an elevated result in a non-canned format is a packaging-integrity signal.

Al.rationale: No credible sovereign sets an aluminium maximum level for a root-vegetable-containing juice. The only sovereign aluminium values in a dietary basis are the packaged-drinking-water quality standards (US 21 CFR 165.110 secondary allowable level 200 ug/kg, EU 2020/2184, Health Canada 2900 ug/kg), which govern water sold as water and are Category 8 instruments, and the FSANZ infant-formula aluminium limits, which are Category 1 and are excluded from this category's anchor set by the taxonomy boundary rule. In this form aluminium is a packaging and processing signal (aluminium cans and can linings, closures, filter aids, additive carry-over) rather than a raw-material contaminant.
Al.reference_method: Total aluminium by ICP-MS on every certified lot, reported on the certificate. A result that departs materially from the applicant's own documented process baseline escalates to a packaging, can-lining and processing-aid investigation. This is a process-control tripwire, not a numeric standard: no ceiling is published because no credible sovereign maximum exists for this cell.

Cr.screen_note: Total chromium is recorded as a SCREEN and not as a protective standalone ceiling: a total-element value in this matrix is dominated by benign Cr(III), while the health-relevant species is Cr(VI). The number is published because a credible sovereign wrote a total-chromium maximum level for the source commodity; the species obligation sits in the Cr-VI cell of this row and in the reflex rule below. This is the same screen treatment total chromium receives in the flavoured-water row.
Cr.binding_control: Total chromium by ICP-MS on every certified lot and reported on the certificate. A result above 250 ug/kg, which is 50 percent of the screen value, or any result that departs materially from the applicant's documented process baseline, triggers the Cr(VI) reflex defined in the Cr-VI cell of this row together with an equipment, process-water and ingredient investigation.
Cr.basis: fresh-weight edible portion of the source vegetable (Hong Kong Cap 132V Part 2 Schedule, which the register records as an as-sold commodity cell), read across to the single-strength juice at face value with no concentration or dilution factor applied; total chromium
Cr.label: Hong Kong Cap 132V Part 2 item 7 sets chromium in vegetables other than pulses at 500 ug/kg, written for total chromium. No credible sovereign has written a chromium maximum level for vegetable juice itself, so the source-commodity cell is adopted by disclosed read-across from the same instrument and on the same logic as this row's cadmium anchor, and it is recorded as a screen.
Cr.substantiation: The candidate set and the rejections. The packaged-drinking-water quality standards (US 21 CFR 165.110 at 100 ug/kg and Hong Kong Cap 132V packaged drinking water at 50 ug/kg) are stricter but govern water sold as water and are Category 8 instruments, and the public-water-system maximum contaminant levels (US EPA, Health Canada) are water-utility instruments rather than food law; neither reaches a single-strength vegetable juice. Within food law the Hong Kong vegetable cell is the only credible sovereign chromium value written for the source commodity of this row, and it is taken as written. Adopting it publishes a sovereign ceiling where this row previously published none and removes nothing: total chromium remains a mandatory lot test and the Cr(VI) reflex continues to bind. No occurrence data selected the number.

companions.basis: food as listed in Cap 132V Part 2 Schedule; source unit mg/kg
companions.scope: Bottled or packaged drinking waters, other than natural mineral waters

Cr-VI.rationale: Hexavalent chromium is not stable in a root-vegetable-containing juice. At the pH of this product form (typically pH 3.8 to 4.8 after the acidification that shelf-stable root-vegetable juices require, with organic acids present) Cr(VI) is reduced to Cr(III) by the organic acids, sugars, ascorbate and polyphenols present in the matrix, so a positive Cr(VI) result is an artifact of the total-chromium determination rather than a species present in the beverage as consumed. The reference-method basis for this determination is the in-house species arbitration at data/workbench/standards/2026-07-31-chromium-formula-adjudication.md, which found that the superseded ion-exchange plus electrothermal-AAS methods that generated the historical Cr(VI) values in liquid food matrices are not reproduced by the modern reference method: saraiva2021 (species-specific isotope dilution HPLC-ICP-MS, limit of quantification 0.049 ug/kg) quantified no Cr(VI) in any milk or formula sample while resolving Cr(III) and total chromium at single-digit ug/kg. That adjudication was drawn on a near-neutral aqueous food matrix; the acidic beverage matrices in this row are a more strongly reducing environment still, so the artifact conclusion carries a fortiori. The health-relevant species is controlled through the total-chromium cell and the reflex rule below, and this determination is a method finding, not an occurrence-derived value: no number is taken from it.
Cr-VI.reference_method: Hexavalent chromium is not a routine lot test. Total chromium (Cr cell) bounds any hexavalent fraction; a Cr(VI)-specific method (IC-ICP-MS, EN 15192 adapted to the liquid matrix) is reflexed where the total-chromium screen is elevated AND the finished-product pH is above 5.0, and a confirmed detection blocks certification pending a process and equipment investigation.
Cr-VI.regulatory_basis: No credible sovereign sets a hexavalent-chromium content limit for any food or beverage; every sovereign chromium value in a dietary or packaged-water basis is written for total chromium (Hong Kong Cap 132V vegetables other than pulses 500 ug/kg, which is this row's total-chromium screen; US 21 CFR 165.110 chromium 100 ug/kg; Hong Kong Cap 132V packaged drinking water 50 ug/kg). Cr(VI) is a species of and bounded by total chromium (Cr-VI <= total Cr).
Cr-VI.jurisdictions_checked: EU 2023/915 (and EU 2024/1987 for nickel, EU 2025/1891 for arsenic in seafood); Codex CXS 193-1995; US FDA (21 CFR 165.110 bottled-water quality standards, Juice HACCP guidance, Closer to Zero action levels); FSANZ Food Standards Code Schedule 19; Health Canada List of Contaminants and Other Adulterating Substances; UK retained maximum levels; Hong Kong Cap 132V (Food Adulteration (Metallic Contamination) Regulations) — none sets a hexavalent-chromium limit for a food or beverage.
